evidence.detail: All 53 authority and 19 authority-claim-compare records have empty governance metadata.

findings.impact: The actual Authority context cannot be deterministically tied back to the Judge case or authority tool_call_id, and the audit fallback misclassifies these Draft records as historical Production diagnostics.
findings.problem: Authority and claim-comparison calls do not produce governed Draft snapshots and use fixed trace IDs instead of the originating Judge trace/case/tool call identity.
findings.remediation: Propagate originating trace_id, case_id, stage, environment hash, and authority tool_call_id into both Authority phases; apply Context Governance before each Authority LLM call and persist segment/tool/output-contract metadata.
verification_evidence: Both Authority phases now use the originating Judge trace and persist trace_id/case_id/tool_call_id lineage in their governance snapshots.

evidence.detail: Evidence fingerprints use the manifest-declared sha256 while the snapshot also includes registration action results such as created/reused/updated.
The enhanced-rules source changed repeatedly during the review; the final revalidation also found field-enums and time-knowledge drift.
53 Authority records contain 10 distinct environment hashes; repeated questions occur under multiple hashes, but compiler/source revision is not recorded in the ContextRecord.

findings.impact: Authority may read changed source content under an identity derived from stale declared hashes, while identical content can receive different identities depending on registry history. Cache and audit evidence are therefore not replay-safe.
findings.problem: environment_snapshot_sha256 is not a stable identity of the evidence actually visible to Authority.
findings.remediation: Fail closed on declared-vs-actual evidence hash mismatch and build the environment hash only from semantic, actual content/tool/permission identities, never registration actions.
verification_evidence: Declared source hashes are checked against actual bytes before materialization; all three changed sources were semantically revalidated and the Investigation gate passed without warnings.
Environment identity now uses registered content fingerprints and excludes create/reuse/update actions; the stability regression test passed.

evidence.detail: basis_evidence_ref_ids and required_evidence are declared as tuple[str, ...].
Schema rendering supports list but not tuple, causing both fields to render as {}.
validate_output accepted basis_evidence_ref_ids='not-an-array' and required_evidence=123 with no errors.
The system prompt manually declares both fields to be string arrays.

findings.impact: Malformed output can pass the official schema and be converted character-by-character during normalization, producing false unresolved results or corrupted required-evidence lists.
findings.problem: The Authority Structured Output schema leaves tuple fields unconstrained, so the handwritten prompt becomes a second output-contract source.
findings.remediation: Add tuple/sequence support to the shared schema and validator, then remove the duplicated field-shape contract from the free-form Authority prompt.
verification_evidence: Shared schema rendering and validation now support tuple and Sequence as JSON arrays, including fixed-length tuples.
tests/test_schema_validator.py passed all 12 tests and the handwritten Authority field-shape contract was removed.

evidence.detail: Missing location metadata and slice materialization errors are appended and skipped.
The errors are stored on AuthorityEnvironment but are not part of the prompt, permission boundary, snapshot, or resolve precondition.

findings.impact: An incomplete evidence space can be interpreted as a business evidence gap and returned as unresolved/gap_only instead of an infrastructure/tool failure.
findings.problem: Some evidence materialization failures are collected in registration_errors but Authority execution proceeds without exposing or enforcing them.
findings.remediation: Fail closed before Authority LLM execution when decision-relevant evidence registration fails, or expose a typed degraded-environment state that AuthorityTool deterministically returns as tool_failure.
verification_evidence: AuthorityEnvironmentInvalid now stops environment construction for materialization errors and source-hash drift before any Authority LLM call.

evidence.detail: AUTHORITY_INTERNAL_TOOL_CALL_LIMIT is 6 and is passed to the LLM client.
The stored conversation contains 13 actual tool calls. Several other records contain 8-11 calls.

findings.impact: Search/Load ordering and context-size constraints may not be hard-enforced, allowing evidence churn and tool-result amplification.
findings.problem: Historical Authority traces exceed the declared six-call internal tool budget, but the records do not preserve enough compiler/runtime identity to prove whether the current version still does so.
findings.remediation: Add deterministic post-run tool-count/order validation and persist the effective runtime/tool-limit version; reproduce on a governed representative Authority case.
verification_evidence: LlmClient now rejects a run when the actual extracted tool-call count exceeds the configured limit.
Authority additionally validates first Search, candidate Search→Load, and navigation load_targets→Load transitions; focused budget and ordering tests passed.

lifecycle_history.reason: Protocol, compiler, lineage, environment and tool-state remediations were implemented pending representative verification.
All five findings have implementation and regression evidence; refreshed Investigation material passed the strict freshness gate.
Verification evidence was archived and all findings exited the blocking set.

objective: Review the Judge-to-Authority context, evidence-space identity, output contract, tool plan, and traceability.
positive_controls: All 53 independent Authority inputs contain only decision_question and environment_snapshot_sha256; claim text is isolated from the independent phase.
All 19 claim-comparison records use a separate caller and contain no tool calls.
Judge exposes authority.resolve only when deterministic candidate reasons exist and declares it as a required governance tool for those Draft cases.
Authority basis references are checked against evidence actually loaded in the current ContextRun.
unresolved: Historical ContextRecords created before this remediation remain non-retroactive: they cannot be uniquely mapped to Judge tool calls because the lineage did not exist at capture time.
